changes_made.explanation: Changed task from 'Text Summarization' to 'Data-to-Text Generation' since the paper focuses on generating text from structured data (box scores). Simplified models list to the three main systems evaluated (Wiseman RNN, Puduppully RNN, Rebuffel transformer) and removed redundant/general terms.
Removed system names and kept only the actual metrics used (Precision, Recall). The systems mentioned are evaluation approaches, not metrics themselves.
Cleaned up empty fields - the paper does not use LLMs as judges.

guideline: Annotators identify factual errors by marking span positions (start/end tokens) and assigning error categories
Annotators identify factual errors by marking span positions (start/end tokens) and assigning error categories
- Each mistake was characterised by its position in the text and a category.

Annotators were instructed to identify factual errors, mark their span (start and end token) and assign one of the predefined categories (Incorrect number, Incorrect name, Incorrect word, Context error, Not checkable, Other).

Annotators were asked to identify factual errors in the text using a defined protocol with categories such as Incorrect number, Incorrect name, Incorrect word, Context error, Not checkable, and Other.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated the lengthy guideline descriptions into a single clear statement. Kept the criteria list as-is since it's already well-normalized.

overall_notes: The paper describes a shared task on evaluating factual accuracy of NLG systems in a sports reporting domain. It focuses on data-to-text generation from basketball box scores. The extraction was generally good but needed normalization of tasks and metrics. The paper evaluates both automatic metrics (precision/recall) and human evaluation protocols.
